review_policy.translation_status: No text here is approved for publication or learner use.
review_policy.back_translation: Independent manual back-translation from each candidate, not checked by a first-language reviewer.
review_policy.hold_rule: Keep earthworks, water-safety, greywater, potable-water, legal, measurement, quantity and sizing instructions in exact English wherever meaning or terminology is uncertain.

candidates.sourceEnglish: Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa.

st.candidate: Dihla tsa dipula di fapana ho pholletsa le Afrika Borwa.
st.backTranslation: The rainy seasons differ throughout South Africa.
st.ambiguity: Check whether 'dihla tsa dipula' is the most familiar local phrasing for rainy seasons.

ve.candidate: Zwifhinga zwa mvula zwi a fhambana kha Afrika Tshipembe.
ve.backTranslation: Rain periods/seasons differ in South Africa.
ve.ambiguity: Check local preference for 'zwifhinga zwa mvula' and the standard written country name.

ts.candidate: Tinguva ta mpfula ta hambana eAfrika Dzonga.
ts.backTranslation: Rainy seasons differ in South Africa.
ts.ambiguity: Check spacing and local style for the country name.

candidates.risk: Low factual risk; geography wording still needs first-language review.

st.candidate: Marulelo a hao a ka bokella metsi a pula.
st.ambiguity: Check the familiar term for roof in the intended Sesotho variety.

ve.candidate: Ṱhanga yaṋu i nga kuvhanganya maḓi a mvula.
ve.ambiguity: The existing Tshivenda draft uses 'mutombo' for roof in a lesson title; a native reviewer should choose the local term and confirm the respectful/plural 'yaṋu'.

ts.candidate: Lwangu ra wena ri nga hlengeleta mati ya mpfula.
ts.ambiguity: Check noun-class agreement and whether 'hlengeleta' is the clearest everyday verb here.

candidates.risk: Low factual risk; roof terminology and agreement need first-language review.

candidates.sourceEnglish: Plan what you will do when stored water runs low.

st.candidate: Rala seo o tla se etsa ha metsi a bolokilweng a qala ho fela.
st.backTranslation: Plan what you will do when saved water starts to run out.
st.ambiguity: Check whether 'metsi a bolokilweng' is a natural way to say stored water and whether 'a qala ho fela' clearly means the supply is getting low.

ve.candidate: Pulani uri ni ḓo ita mini musi maḓi o vhulungwaho a tshi fhungudzea.
ve.backTranslation: Plan what you will do when stored water becomes less.
ve.ambiguity: Check 'pulani' as an everyday imperative and confirm that 'a tshi fhungudzea' conveys a low remaining supply, rather than any decrease.

ts.candidate: Kunguhata leswi u nga ta swi endla loko mati lama hlayisiweke ma hunguteka.
ts.backTranslation: Plan what you will do when the stored water decreases.
ts.ambiguity: Check whether 'ma hunguteka' naturally conveys that only a little water remains.

candidates.risk: Moderate meaning risk: 'runs low' is relative, not 'is completely finished'. Confirm this distinction before use.
